title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative:
The ICSP Programme, implemented by Trócaire and partners in Rwanda, works towards the goal that poor and marginalised people, especially women and youth, have sustainable livelihoods and diverse food sources. This objective supports people living in poverty to collaborate in advocacy initiatives for their rights. Activities will focus on local and national level dialogues, supporting evidence-based climate change advocacy at national/regional/international levels; participation in national/regional climate networks, and other preparations for participation in major climate events e.g. COP. The principal focus of this outcome is: Supporting communities to • establish themselves as recognised authorities for rehabilitation, protection and management or co-management (with local and national authorities) of their common resources including water, forest, wetlands ecosystems. • To track local government budgets for governance and management of natural resources • To implement evidence-based environmental and climate change advocacy; supporting local voices to advocate for the protection of their natural resources; influencing national and international policy and decision makers on food, agriculture, climate and environmental justice policies and strategies at local and national levels. Examples include rights to diverse seeds, access to services, land, water and wildlife.
Supporting women and women centred organisations to • To form their own structures and gain skills to participate in food rights, seed rights, environmental and climate networks and advocacy groups.
